root_idea.summary: The root centers on something leaving active awareness: failing to retain or recall it, and, by extension, leaving or disregarding it.
root_idea.development: The lexical evidence distinguishes forgetfulness after something was present to the mind from deliberate abandonment or neglect. Quranic usage extends the latter to culpable human disregard and to divine retributive abandonment. The separately hamzated family associated with postponement is not treated as a direct meaning of this root.

senses.definition: To forget; to lose the active remembrance of something previously known, entrusted, or present to the mind.
senses.usage_conditions: This covers ordinary lapses of recollection and failure to retain what one has been reminded of. The Quranic form can also occur where the forgetting has an intentional or culpable basis, treated separately below.

senses.definition: To deliberately neglect, disregard, or leave something unheeded.
senses.usage_conditions: In culpable human conduct, forgetting may mean intentionally abandoning what was entrusted or commanded. When attributed to God, the expression denotes leaving people in disregard or abandonment as requital, not a loss of divine knowledge.

senses.definition: To cause someone to forget; to make something forgotten by removing its remembrance from the mind.
senses.usage_conditions: The causative construction may take a person who is made to forget or a matter whose remembrance is caused to disappear, including the erasure of a matter from people's hearts by divine power.
In the expression نَسْيًا مَنْسِيًّا, the passive participle reinforces the status of something treated as forgotten and of little account.
An adjectival use describing one marked by forgetfulness, distinct from the passive-participial sense of مَنْسِيّ, “forgotten.”

senses.definition: A thing of little account; something left behind or liable to be forgotten.
senses.usage_conditions: The noun can denote what receives little consideration, even when it has not literally been forgotten. In the Quranic expression نَسْيًا مَنْسِيًّا, it describes something treated as negligible and forgotten.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Plural terms for women, serving as plurals of امرأة by forms different from the singular.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are lexically distinct plural terms, not forms of the Quranic verb meaning “to forget.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bodily vein or cord known as al-nasā, traditionally located in the thigh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical anatomical usage also reports dual and plural variants of the term.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer-only unit: “See نسو”; it supplies no lexical definition for this root.

cautions: The Quranic Form I expressions attributed to God use “forgetting” figuratively for leaving or disregarding people in requital, rather than implying loss of knowledge.
The supplied Maqayis discussion distinguishes the unhamzated root نسي from hamzated forms such as نَسَأ associated with postponement; those meanings are not assigned here.
